title: Officer lied at inquest; RCMP boss suspends constable, orders probe into death
article: The RCMP officer who shot and killed an unarmed man in a Vanderhoof playing field more than three years ago was suspended indefinitely yesterday and could face criminal charges for lying at the coroner's inquest into the death of Kevin St. Arnaud.

The RCMP held a press conference at its B.C. headquarters to announce the action taken against Const. Ryan Sheremetta, who shot St. Arnaud, 29, three times on the playing field of Nechako Valley Secondary School on Dec. 19, 2004.

"The issue is that Const. Sheremetta did conduct himself in a disgraceful manner that could bring discredit to the force by knowingly making false, misleading or inaccurate statements while testifying at the coroner's inquest into the death of Kevin St. Arnaud," said Assistant Commissioner Al Macintyre.

Sheremetta, who was transferred to the Kamloops detachment, was reassigned to administrative duties in August 2007 during the course of the investigation by the Commission for Public Complaints in conjunction with a senior RCMP investigator.
He was informed of his suspension with pay under the RCMP Act yesterday, but the force has also launched a process to suspend the officer without pay.
"The suspension is a process to remove him from the law enforcement with the police department while this matter continues on," said Macintyre.

Sheremetta was in his mid-20s and had about two years' experience when he shot St. Arnaud. According to police at the time, St. Arnaud, who was intoxicated, was shot after a burglar alarm went off following a break-in.
Macintyre said the RCMP has forwarded its findings to Crown counsel for charge approval, possibly for perjury, after an extensive internal and criminal investigation.
RCMP spokesman Staff Sgt. John Ward said officers must never lie under oath.
"It's a matter that by law we have to tell the truth under oath," said Ward.
B.C.'s chief coroner was told of the findings and could reconvene the inquest.
The RCMP has asked the Toronto Metropolitan Police Service to conduct an independent review of the investigation into the case.
"They will look at the whole thing from start to finish," said Macintyre.
